label: copy phase: fed-back i/a/o/n/r/g after the first output
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L). It never fires in the original phase, on <DEL>, at recall_idx 0, or on the first occurrence of a token (all activations have in_first=0). Activation depends mostly on the fed-back input token. It is strongest on i, a, o (about 28-30% active, roughly 63% of the mass), then n and r (about 17%), then g. Other letters fire weakly and rarely, and digits almost never. Rates are highest at recall_idx 2-4 (absolute t 10-12) and pick up again near the end of long L=9 sequences. Within a sequence, activation tends to run as a decaying stretch across early copy steps. Many i/a/o inputs do not fire, so precision is about 0.53. Requiring recall_idx >= 2 is the main refinement; adding conditions on absolute t, prev_tok, or in_count did not help.
